candidates.statement: I. INTRODUCTION This guidance is intended to assist requestors 2 in preparing over-the-counter (OTC) monograph order requests (OMORs) 3 for submission to FDA under section 505G of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) (21 U.S.C. 355h). This guidance provides FDA’s recommendations on the format and content of the information that requestors should provide in an OMOR and identifies relevant guidance documents to assist requestors in preparing their OMORs. However, because the type and quantity of data and information that would support a determination that a particular drug is generally recognized as safe and effective (GRASE) or a change to a condition of use of a drug is GRASE may vary, not all of the information described in this guidance may be relevant to each particular OMOR.
candidates.context: To discuss an alternative approach, contact the FDA office responsible for this guidance as listed on the title page. In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities.

candidates.statement: Either FDA or a requestor can initiate the order process. A requestor can initiate the order process by submitting an OMOR with respect to certain drugs, classes of drugs, or combinations of drugs. 4 The OMOR may request issuance of an order determining the following: (1) whether a drug is GRASE or (2) whether a change to a condition of use of a drug is GRASE. 5 The OMOR must be submitted to FDA in the form and manner specified by the Agency. 6 FDA will file the OMOR if FDA determines that the OMOR is sufficiently complete and formatted to permit FDA to conduct a substantive review. 7
candidates.context: Under the process set forth in section 505G(b) of the FD&C Act, FDA has the authority to issue a final order that adds, removes, or changes GRASE conditions for an OTC monograph drug. candidates.statement: FDA has issued guidance documents specific to CTD 10 for organizing certain applications that will be submitted to FDA. The recommendations provided in these guidance documents are also applicable to OMORs. Although, in general, requestors should follow the recommendations provided in previously issued CTD guidance documents, this guidance highlights additional format and content recommendations specific to OMORs.
candidates.context: A. General Considerations The CTD is designed for multiple types of regulatory applications. The CTD is sufficiently flexible to accommodate the types and sources of information that may be included in OMORs. The type and quantity of data and information capable of demonstrating that a drug or change to a condition of use of a drug is GRASE is specific to each OMOR. For example, the type and quantity of the data and information may vary depending on the request and whether the OMOR is a Tier 1 OMOR 11 or a Tier 2 OMOR. 12 Therefore, an OMOR may not include all the information identified for certain modules, section headings, or subsection headings described in this guidance or other CTD guidance documents if it is not applicable to that specific OMOR. In those circumstances, the requestor should indicate that no information is being submitted for a given module, section heading, or subse

candidates.context: FDA has issued guidance documents specific to CTD 10 for organizing certain applications that will be submitted to FDA. The recommendations provided in these guidance documents are also applicable to OMORs. Although, in general, requestors should follow the recommendations provided in previously issued CTD guidance documents, this guidance highlights additional format and content recommendations specific to OMORs. Because the type and quantity of data and information to support a GRASE determination is specific to each OMOR, FDA encourages requestors to request a formal meeting with FDA to discuss the overall data recommendations before the initiation of an OMOR development program and during the course of the OMOR development program. 13 FDA also encourages requestors to request a meeting with FDA before the submission of an OMOR.

Introduction to the summary documents The Introduction to the Summary Documents section should provide a concise narrative summary of (1) the positive safety and effectiveness data supporting a determination that a specific drug, class of drugs, or combination of drugs with the proposed active ingredient or other condition is GRASE for the intended nonprescription use and (2) the negative safety and effectiveness data that are not supportive of a determination that the specific drug, class of drugs, or combination of drugs or other condition is GRASE. The introduction should clearly identify and address each of the major topics addressed in the submission. The introduction should include a summary table listing all studies included in the submission with their corresponding titles (as they appear in the study reports), study numbers, and location in the submission. candidates.statement: c. Nonclinical overview The Nonclinical Overview section should present an integrated and critical assessment of the pharmacological, pharmacokinetic, and toxicological evaluation of the active ingredient or other conditions. Where relevant guidances on the conduct of studies exist, requestors should take these guidances into consideration and discuss any deviation from the recommendations in these guidances. The nonclinical testing strategy should be discussed and justified. There should be comments on the good laboratory practice status of the studies submitted, taking into consideration which studies are pivotal to support the safety of the active ingredient. Requestors should indicate any association between nonclinical findings and the quality assessment, the results of clinical studies, or the effects seen with related drug products or ingredients, as appropriate.

candidates.context: IV. OTHER CONSIDERATIONS FOR AN OMOR B. Fonts Font size for text and tables should be of a style and size that is large enough to be easily legible, even after photocopying or when provided electronically. We recommend that narrative text be submitted in Times New Roman 12-point font. Generally, font sizes 9 to 10 points are considered acceptable in tables, but requestors should avoid fonts smaller than 12 points whenever possible. When choosing a font size for tables, it is important to balance the desirability of providing sufficient information on a single page to facilitate data comparisons with that of maintaining a font size that remains readable. If the font size is too large, data comparisons may be complicated because data may be presented in multiple tables. We recommend 10-point font for footnotes.

Generally, font sizes 9 to 10 points are considered acceptable in tables, but requestors should avoid fonts smaller than 12 points whenever possible. When choosing a font size for tables, it is important to balance the desirability of providing sufficient information on a single page to facilitate data comparisons with that of maintaining a font size that remains readable. If the font size is too large, data comparisons may be complicated because data may be presented in multiple tables. We recommend 10-point font for footnotes. D. candidates.statement: D. Pagination Page numbering should be at the document level and not at the module level. The entire submission should never be numbered consecutively by page. In general, all documents should have page numbers. Because the page numbering is at the document level, there should only be one set of page numbers for each document.
candidates.context: C. Paper Size Generally, the requestor should format an OMOR to standard U.S. letter size paper (8.5 by 11 inches). Occasionally, a requestor may format individual pages larger than standard paper size to present a floor plan, synthesis diagram, batch formula, or manufacturing instructions. If the OMOR includes a document within a document, such as a protocol within a study report, the document to be included (in this case, the protocol) should be attached as an appendix.

ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT The National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (NEPA) requires all federal agencies to assess the environmental impacts of their actions and to ensure that the interested and affected public is informed of environmental analyses. FDA complies with NEPA by evaluating environmental impacts of agency action, such as decisions on applications or petitions, as a part of its regulatory process.

candidates.statement: In general, until disclosure is triggered under section 505G(d)(2) of the FD&C Act, any information, including reports of testing conducted on the drug or drugs involved, that is submitted by a requestor in connection with proceedings on an order under section 505G of the FD&C Act and is a trade secret or confidential information subject to 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4) or 18 U.S.C. 1905 will not be disclosed to the public unless the requestor consents to that disclosure. 66 However, FDA generally must make any information submitted by a requestor in support of an OMOR (e.g., the contents of the OMOR) available to the public not later than the date on which the proposed order is issued. 67 Nonetheless, the information will remain confidential if (1) the information pertains to pharmaceutical quality information, unless such information is necessary to establish standards under which a drug is GRASE; (2) the information is of the type contained in raw datasets; (3) the information is submitted in a requestor-initiated request, but the requestor withdraws the request in accordance with withdrawal procedures established by FDA before FDA issues the proposed order; or (4) FDA requests and obtains the information under section 505G(c) of the FD&C Act and the information is not submitted in relation to an order under section 505G(b) of the FD&C Act. 68
